$$\begin{align*}(y-2)(y-5)&=0\\y-2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad y-5=0\\y&=2\quad\text{or}\quad y=5\end{align*}$$
For $y=2$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=2^2-7(2)+10\\\mathrm{LHS}&=0=\mathrm{RHS}\end{align*}$$
For $y=5$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=5^2-7(5)+10\\\mathrm{LHS}&=0=\mathrm{RHS}\end{align*}$$
Both solutions check.

$$\begin{align*}(b+1)(b-14)&=0\\b+1&=0\quad\text{or}\quad b-14=0\\b&=-1\quad\text{or}\quad b=14\end{align*}$$
For $b=-1$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=(-1)^2-13(-1)-14\\\mathrm{LHS}&=0=\mathrm{RHS}\end{align*}$$
For $b=14$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=14^2-13(14)-14\\\mathrm{LHS}&=0=\mathrm{RHS}\end{align*}$$
Both solutions check.

$$\begin{align*}(z+3)(z-30)&=0\\z+3&=0\quad\text{or}\quad z-30=0\\z&=-3\quad\text{or}\quad z=30\end{align*}$$
For $z=-3$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=(-3)^2-27(-3)-90\\\mathrm{LHS}&=0=\mathrm{RHS}\end{align*}$$
For $z=30$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=30^2-27(30)-90\\\mathrm{LHS}&=0=\mathrm{RHS}\end{align*}$$
Both solutions check.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+x-90&=0\\(x+10)(x-9)&=0\\x+10&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-9=0\\x&=-10\quad\text{or}\quad x=9\end{align*}$$
For $x=-10$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=(-10)^2+(-10)\\\mathrm{LHS}&=90\\\mathrm{RHS}&=90\end{align*}$$
For $x=9$:
$$\begin{align*}\mathrm{LHS}&=9^2+9\\\mathrm{LHS}&=90\\\mathrm{RHS}&=90\end{align*}$$
Both solutions give LHS = RHS.

answer.worked:
For $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+5x&=14\\x^2+5x-14&=0\\(x+7)(x-2)&=0\\x+7&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-2=0\\x&=-7\quad\text{or}\quad x=2\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}15&=x(x-2)\\x^2-2x-15&=0\\(x+3)(x-5)&=0\\x+3&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-5=0\\x&=-3\quad\text{or}\quad x=5\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}6-x^2&=x\\x^2+x-6&=0\\(x+3)(x-2)&=0\\x+3&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-2=0\\x&=-3\quad\text{or}\quad x=2\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+6&=7x\\x^2-7x+6&=0\\(x-1)(x-6)&=0\\x-1&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-6=0\\x&=1\quad\text{or}\quad x=6\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2+32&=18x\\x^2-18x+32&=0\\(x-2)(x-16)&=0\\x-2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-16=0\\x&=2\quad\text{or}\quad x=16\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $3x$.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+1)&=30\\x^2+x-30&=0\\(x+6)(x-5)&=0\\x+6&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-5=0\\x&=-6\quad\text{or}\quad x=5\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $4x$.
$$\begin{align*}x(x+1)&=20\\x^2+x-20&=0\\(x+5)(x-4)&=0\\x+5&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-4=0\\x&=-5\quad\text{or}\quad x=4\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $x$.
$$\begin{align*}x^2-14&=5x\\x^2-5x-14&=0\\(x+2)(x-7)&=0\\x+2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-7=0\\x&=-2\quad\text{or}\quad x=7\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne-1,0$, multiply by $6x(x+1)$.
$$\begin{align*}6x&=(5x-6)(x+1)\\6x&=5x^2-x-6\\5x^2-7x-6&=0\\5x^2-10x+3x-6&=0\\5x(x-2)+3(x-2)&=0\\(5x+3)(x-2)&=0\\5x+3&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-2=0\\x&=-\frac35\quad\text{or}\quad x=2\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne\frac32$, multiply by $3(2x-3)$.
$$\begin{align*}(2x+1)(2x-3)&=-(51+32x)\\4x^2-4x-3&=-51-32x\\4x^2+28x+48&=0\\x^2+7x+12&=0\\(x+4)(x+3)&=0\\x+4&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x+3=0\\x&=-4\quad\text{or}\quad x=-3\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $6x$.
$$\begin{align*}6x^2+6&=13x\\6x^2-13x+6&=0\\6x^2-9x-4x+6&=0\\3x(2x-3)-2(2x-3)&=0\\(3x-2)(2x-3)&=0\\3x-2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad 2x-3=0\\x&=\frac23\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac32\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0,1,2$, multiply by $x(x-1)(x-2)$.
$$\begin{align*}3x(x-2)&=(3x-2)(x-1)\\3x^2-6x&=3x^2-5x+2\\-6x&=-5x+2\\-x&=2\\x&=-2\end{align*}$$
This value satisfies the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply by $5x$.
$$\begin{align*}x(35-4x)&=36-5x\\35x-4x^2&=36-5x\\4x^2-40x+36&=0\\x^2-10x+9&=0\\(x-1)(x-9)&=0\\x-1&=0\quad\text{or}\quad x-9=0\\x&=1\quad\text{or}\quad x=9\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

For $x\ne0$, multiply both sides by $x$.

For $x\ne0$, multiply both sides by $x$.

For $x\ne1$, multiply both sides by $x-1$.

For $x\ne-\frac32$, isolate the fraction and multiply by $2x+3$.

answer.worked:
The restriction is $x\ne0$. Multiply both sides by $15x$.
$$\begin{align*}10x^2+x(x-1)&=10x+330\\11x^2-11x-330&=0\\x^2-x-30&=0\\(x+5)(x-6)&=0\\x&=-5\text{ or }x=6\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

The restriction is $x\ne4$, so $\dfrac{x-4}{x-4}=1$.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{x}{2}+1&=\frac{x}{3}\\3x+6&=2x\\x&=-6\end{align*}$$
This value satisfies the original equation.

The restriction is $x\ne2$. Multiply both sides by $7(x-2)$.
$$\begin{align*}(x+1)(x-2)+56&=21(x-2)\\x^2-x+54&=21x-42\\x^2-22x+96&=0\\(x-6)(x-16)&=0\\x&=6\text{ or }x=16\end{align*}$$
Both values satisfy the original equation.

The restrictions are $x\ne-2,4$. Multiply both sides by $3(x+2)(x-4)$.
$$\begin{align*}3(x-1)(x-4)-3(x-3)(x+2)&=-2(x+2)(x-4)\\3(x^2-5x+4)-3(x^2-x-6)&=-2(x^2-2x-8)\\-12x+30&=-2x^2+4x+16\\2x^2-16x+14&=0\\x^2-8x+7&=0\\(x-1)(x-7)&=0\\x&=1\text{ or }x=7\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}x^2+8x+16-16+18&=0\\(x+4)^2+2&=0\\(x+4)^2&=-2\end{align*}$$
Since $(x+4)^2\geq0$ for every real $x$, there is no real solution.

$$\begin{align*}x^2-4x+4-4+6&=0\\(x-2)^2+2&=0\\(x-2)^2&=-2\end{align*}$$
Since $(x-2)^2\geq0$ for every real $x$, there is no real solution.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+2x+1-1+4&=0\\(x+1)^2+3&=0\\(x+1)^2&=-3\end{align*}$$

$$\begin{align*}x^2+x+\frac14-\frac14+2&=0\\\left(x+\frac12\right)^2+\frac74&=0\\\left(x+\frac12\right)^2&=-\frac74\end{align*}$$
Since $\left(x+\frac12\right)^2\geq0$ for every real $x$, there is no real solution.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+2x+1-1+2&=0\\(x+1)^2+1&=0\\(x+1)^2&=-1\end{align*}$$
Since $(x+1)^2\geq0$ for every real $x$, there is no real solution.

$$\begin{align*}x^2+4x+4-4+5&=0\\(x+2)^2+1&=0\\(x+2)^2&=-1\end{align*}$$

answer.worked: In $y=(x-0)^2-1$, $h=0$ and $k=-1$. The turning point is $(0,-1)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$.
In $y=(x-1)^2+0$, $h=1$ and $k=0$. The turning point is $(1,0)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=1$.
Write $x+2=x-(-2)$, so $h=-2$ and $k=-1$. The turning point is $(-2,-1)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=-2$.
In $y=(x-0)^2+4$, $h=0$ and $k=4$. The turning point is $(0,4)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=0$.
Write $x+3=x-(-3)$, so $h=-3$ and $k=0$. The turning point is $(-3,0)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=-3$.
Write $x+1=x-(-1)$, so $h=-1$ and $k=2$. The turning point is $(-1,2)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=-1$.
Here $h=2$ and $k=-2$. The turning point is $(2,-2)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=2$.
Write $y=(x-1)^2+3$, so $h=1$ and $k=3$. The turning point is $(1,3)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=1$.
Write $y=(x-3)^2-2$, so $h=3$ and $k=-2$. The turning point is $(3,-2)$ and the axis of symmetry is $x=3$.

content.prompt: Solve the following:

answer.short:
$x=-\dfrac89$.

Isolate the radical, square, factorise and check candidates in the original equation.
answer.worked:
Require $x\geq-1$ and $x+\sqrt{x+1}\ne0$. Cross-multiplying gives
$$\begin{align*}5x-5\sqrt{x+1}&=11x+11\sqrt{x+1}\\6x&=-16\sqrt{x+1}\\3x&=-8\sqrt{x+1}.\end{align*}$$
The right-hand side is nonpositive, so $x\leq0$. Squaring gives
$$\begin{align*}9x^2&=64(x+1)\\9x^2-64x-64&=0\\9x^2-72x+8x-64&=0\\9x(x-8)+8(x-8)&=0\\(9x+8)(x-8)&=0\\x&=-\frac89\quad\text{or}\quad x=8.\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=8$, since it does not satisfy $x\leq0$. For $x=-\frac89$, $\sqrt{x+1}=\frac13$ and
$$\frac{-\frac89-\frac13}{-\frac89+\frac13}=\frac{-\frac{11}{9}}{-\frac59}=\frac{11}{5}.$$
Hence $x=-\frac89$.

answer.short:
$x=2$; $x=\dfrac12$ is excluded.

Cross-multiply, factorise and reject values that make an original denominator zero.
answer.worked:
Since $2x^2+5x-3=(2x-1)(x+3)$, require $x\ne\frac12,-3$. Cross-multiplying gives
$$\begin{align*}2x^2+5x-3&=(2x+1)(2x-1)\\2x^2+5x-3&=4x^2-1\\2x^2-5x+2&=0\\2x^2-4x-x+2&=0\\2x(x-2)-(x-2)&=0\\(2x-1)(x-2)&=0\\x&=\frac12\quad\text{or}\quad x=2.\end{align*}$$
Reject $x=\frac12$, which makes both original denominators zero. For $x=2$,
$$\mathrm{LHS}=\frac13,\qquad \mathrm{RHS}=\frac{5}{8+10-3}=\frac13.$$
Hence $x=2$.

content.prompt:
While wrapping his son’s Christmas present, which is in the shape of a rectangular box, a parent notices that if the length of the box was increased by 2 cm, the width increased by 3 cm and the height increased by 4 cm, the box would become a cube and its volume would be increased by $1207\text{ cm}^3$.

Find the length of the edge of the resulting cube and the dimensions of the box.

answer.short:
Cube edge: $13\text{ cm}$. Box: $11\text{ cm}\times10\text{ cm}\times9\text{ cm}$.

Express the box dimensions using the cube edge and equate the increase in volume to $1207\text{ cm}^3$.
answer.worked:
Let the cube edge be $x$ cm. The box has length $(x-2)$ cm, width $(x-3)$ cm and height $(x-4)$ cm, so $x>4$.

$$\begin{align*}x^3-(x-2)(x-3)(x-4)&=1207\\x^3-(x^2-5x+6)(x-4)&=1207\\x^3-(x^3-9x^2+26x-24)&=1207\\9x^2-26x+24&=1207\\9x^2-26x-1183&=0\\9x^2-117x+91x-1183&=0\\9x(x-13)+91(x-13)&=0\\(x-13)(9x+91)&=0\end{align*}$$

By the null factor law, $x=13$ or $x=-\frac{91}{9}$. Since $x>4$, the cube edge is $13$ cm.

The original box has length $13-2=11$ cm, width $13-3=10$ cm and height $13-4=9$ cm.

Check: $13^3-11\times10\times9=2197-990=1207\text{ cm}^3$.

content.prompt:
A gardener decides to subdivide a rectangular garden bed of area $30\text{ m}^2$ into three equal sections.

He places edging along the outside of the garden bed and as dividers between each section. It takes $32\text{ m}$ of edging. Each section of garden has length $y$ metres (which is also the length of each divider) and width $x$ metres.

spec.sourceRegion: Challenge exercise question 4, diagram to the right of the stem
spec.description: Unshaded rectangle divided by two full-height vertical lines into three adjacent equal sections. Each top segment is labelled x m; the right side is labelled y m. Source blue ordinary strokes are rendered black under house style.
spec.mathematics: The whole garden has dimensions 3x by y. Its outside boundary and two internal dividers require 6x+4y metres of edging.
spec.answerVisibility: All outlines, dividers and dimension labels are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Express the area of the entire garden bed in terms of $x$.

answer.worked:
The edging includes two horizontal sides and four lengths of $y$.

$$\begin{align*}6x+4y&=32\\4y&=32-6x\\y&=8-\frac32x\end{align*}$$
The whole garden has width $3x$, so its area in square metres is
$$\begin{align*}A&=3xy\\A&=3x\left(8-\frac32x\right)\\A&=24x-\frac92x^2\\A&=\frac12(48x-9x^2).\end{align*}$$

children.label: b
children.prompt: Find the dimensions of the garden bed.

answer.short:
$10\text{ m}\times3\text{ m}$ or $6\text{ m}\times5\text{ m}$.

Set the area expression equal to $30$, factorise and use both positive solutions.
answer.worked:
Using the area of $30\text{ m}^2$,
$$\begin{align*}\frac12(48x-9x^2)&=30\\48x-9x^2&=60\\9x^2-48x+60&=0\\3x^2-16x+20&=0\\3x^2-10x-6x+20&=0\\x(3x-10)-2(3x-10)&=0\\(x-2)(3x-10)&=0\end{align*}$$
By the null factor law,
$$\begin{align*}x-2&=0\quad\text{or}\quad3x-10=0\\x&=2\quad\text{or}\quad x=\frac{10}{3}.\end{align*}$$
If $x=2$,
$$\begin{align*}3x&=6\\y&=8-\frac32(2)\\y&=5.\end{align*}$$
If $x=\frac{10}{3}$,
$$\begin{align*}3x&=10\\y&=8-\frac32\left(\frac{10}{3}\right)\\y&=3.\end{align*}$$
The garden bed is $6\text{ m}\times5\text{ m}$ or $10\text{ m}\times3\text{ m}$. Both have area $30\text{ m}^2$. Their edging totals are respectively $2(6)+4(5)=32\text{ m}$ and $2(10)+4(3)=32\text{ m}$.

content.prompt: A rectangular lawn $a$ metres long and $b$ metres wide has a path of uniform width $x$ metres around it.

spec.description: Unshaded inner lawn and outer rectangular boundary, separated by a uniform external path. Dimension arrows show the inner dimensions a m and b m, and the right-hand path width x with a dotted leader. Decorative source blue outlines and red leader are rendered black.
spec.mathematics: The lawn is a by b; the outside rectangle is (a+2x) by (b+2x). Equal inset distances represent uniform width without supplying the derived outside dimensions.
spec.answerVisibility: All diagram labels are permanent givens; no answers are shown.

children.label: a
children.prompt: Find the area of the path in terms of $a$, $b$ and $x$.

answer.worked:
The outside dimensions are $(a+2x)$ m and $(b+2x)$ m. Subtract the lawn area from the outside area:
$$\begin{align*}A_{\text{path}}&=(a+2x)(b+2x)-ab\\A_{\text{path}}&=ab+2ax+2bx+4x^2-ab\\A_{\text{path}}&=2ax+2bx+4x^2.\end{align*}$$
The area is $(2ax+2bx+4x^2)\,\mathrm{m}^2$.

children.prompt: Find the area of the path in terms of $x$.

children.label: ii
children.prompt: If the area of the path is $160\,\mathrm{m}^2$, find the value of $x$.

answer.worked:
$$\begin{align*}4x^2+156x&=160\\4x^2+156x-160&=0\\x^2+39x-40&=0\\(x+40)(x-1)&=0\\x&=-40\quad\text{or}\quad x=1.\end{align*}$$
The width is positive, so reject $x=-40$. Hence $x=1$, giving a path width of $1\,\mathrm{m}$.

Check: $4(1)^2+156(1)=160\,\mathrm{m}^2$.

spec.description: Unshaded convex pentagon with cyclic vertices A, B, C, D, E; EA is horizontal. Only diagonal AD is drawn, dashed and red. Ordinary source-blue boundary lines become black under house style.
spec.mathematics: AD joins two non-adjacent vertices of pentagon ABCDE.
spec.answerVisibility: All geometry and labels are permanent givens.

answer.worked: Each of the 4 vertices joins to 1 non-adjacent vertex. Each diagonal is counted twice, so the number of diagonals is $4\times1\div2=2$.
Each of the 5 vertices joins to 2 non-adjacent vertices. Dividing by 2 to avoid counting each diagonal twice gives $5\times2\div2=5$ diagonals.
Each of the 6 vertices joins to 3 non-adjacent vertices. Dividing by 2 to avoid counting each diagonal twice gives $6\times3\div2=9$ diagonals.
Each of the 10 vertices joins to 7 non-adjacent vertices. Dividing by 2 to avoid counting each diagonal twice gives $10\times7\div2=35$ diagonals.
Each of the 20 vertices joins to 17 non-adjacent vertices. Dividing by 2 to avoid counting each diagonal twice gives $20\times17\div2=170$ diagonals.

children.label: b
children.prompt: Explain why the number of diagonals in an $n$-sided polygon is $\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}$.

answer.short: Each of the $n$ vertices joins to $n-3$ non-adjacent vertices. Each diagonal is counted twice, so there are $\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}$ diagonals.
answer.worked: From each vertex, exclude the vertex itself and its two adjacent vertices, leaving $n-3$ possible diagonal endpoints. Across all $n$ vertices this gives $n(n-3)$ counts. Every diagonal is counted from both endpoints, so divide by 2: $\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: A particular polygon has 405 diagonals. How many sides does it have?

answer.worked:
Let $n$ be the number of sides.
$$\begin{align*}\frac{n(n-3)}{2}&=405\\n(n-3)&=810\\n^2-3n-810&=0\\(n-30)(n+27)&=0\\n&=30\text{ or }n=-27\end{align*}$$
The number of sides is positive, so the polygon has 30 sides. Check: $30\times27\div2=405$ diagonals.

children.label: d
children.prompt: What polygon has between 1900 and 2000 diagonals?

answer.short:
A 64-gon.

Use $\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}$ and check neighbouring whole numbers of sides.
answer.worked:
Let $D(n)=\dfrac{n(n-3)}{2}$ be the number of diagonals. As the whole number $n$ increases, the number of diagonals increases. Since $n(n-3)$ is near $4000$ and $\sqrt{4000}$ is near 63, test nearby whole numbers:
$$\begin{align*}D(63)&=\frac{63\times60}{2}=1890\\D(64)&=\frac{64\times61}{2}=1952\\D(65)&=\frac{65\times62}{2}=2015\end{align*}$$
Only 1952 is between 1900 and 2000, so the polygon is a 64-gon.

content.prompt: At a party, each guest shakes hands with each other guest.

children.label: a
children.prompt: How many hand shakes are there if there are:

answer.worked: Each guest shakes hands with the other guest; this is one pair, so there is 1 hand shake.

Count each pair once: the first guest shakes hands with 2 others, and the second has 1 remaining hand shake.

$2+1=3$ hand shakes.
Count each pair once: $3+2+1=6$ hand shakes.

Each of 10 guests shakes hands with 9 others. This counts every hand shake twice.

$\dfrac{10\times9}{2}=45$ hand shakes.

children.label: b
children.prompt: At a party with $n$ guests, explain why there are $\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$ hand shakes.

answer.short: Each of the $n$ guests shakes hands with $n-1$ others. The product $n(n-1)$ counts every hand shake twice, so divide by 2.
answer.worked: For each of the $n$ guests there are $n-1$ other guests, giving $n(n-1)$ counts. Each hand shake is counted once for each of its two participants. Therefore the number of hand shakes is $\dfrac{n(n-1)}{2}$.

children.label: c
children.prompt: At Bill’s party there were 190 hand shakes. How many people were at the party?

answer.short:
20 people.

Use the handshake formula and solve the resulting quadratic, keeping the positive solution.
answer.worked:
Let $n$ be the number of people.

$$\begin{align*}\frac{n(n-1)}{2}&=190\\n(n-1)&=380\\n^2-n-380&=0\\(n-20)(n+19)&=0\\n&=20\text{ or }n=-19\end{align*}$$

The number of people is positive, so there were 20 people.

Check: $\dfrac{20\times19}{2}=190$ hand shakes.

content.prompt: A right-angled triangle has a hypotenuse of length $41\text{ cm}$ and an area of $180\text{ cm}^2$. What are the lengths of the other two sides?

answer.short:
$9\text{ cm}$ and $40\text{ cm}$.

Use the area and Pythagoras to find the sum and product of the two lengths, then solve a quadratic.
answer.worked:
Let the perpendicular sides have lengths $a\text{ cm}$ and $b\text{ cm}$, where $a,b>0$.

The area gives
$$\begin{align*}\frac12 ab&=180\\ab&=360.\end{align*}$$
Pythagoras gives $a^2+b^2=41^2=1681$. Hence
$$\begin{align*}(a+b)^2&=a^2+b^2+2ab\\(a+b)^2&=1681+720\\(a+b)^2&=2401\\a+b&=49.\end{align*}$$
Thus $b=49-a$, so
$$\begin{align*}a(49-a)&=360\\49a-a^2&=360\\a^2-49a+360&=0\\(a-9)(a-40)&=0.\end{align*}$$
Therefore $a=9$ or $a=40$; the corresponding value of $b$ is $40$ or $9$.

Check: $9^2+40^2=1681=41^2$ and $\frac12\times9\times40=180$.

The other two sides are $9\text{ cm}$ and $40\text{ cm}$.

entries.description:
Solution of simple quadratic equations
• To solve a quadratic equation:
– If there is a numerical common factor, divide both sides of the equation by the factor.
– Move all terms to the left-hand side of the equation, leaving zero on the right-hand side.

2n² + 15n − 12n − 90 = 0
n(2n + 15) − 6(2n + 15) = 0
(2n + 15)(n − 6) = 0
2n + 15 = 0 or n − 6 = 0
n = −15/2 or n = 6

y = (0 − 1)² − 3
  = 1 − 3

∴ x = 1 + √3 or x = 1 − √3
(1 + √3, 0) and (1 − √3, 0) are x-intercepts.

entries.description:
y = x² + 4x − 5. (Convert to the form y = (x − h)² + k.)
y = x² + 4x + (4/2)² − (4/2)² − 5
= (x² + 4x + 4) − 4 − 5
= (x + 2)² − 9
The turning point is (−2, −9).
When x = 0, y = −5.
The y-intercept is (0, −5).
When y = 0,
0 = (x + 2)² − 9
∴ (x + 2)² = 9
∴ x + 2 = 3 or x + 2 = −3
∴ x = 1 or x = −5
The x-intercepts are (1, 0) and (−5, 0).
